text.p: - President Milan Kucan held talks with the governor of the Bank of Slovenia France Arhar and the president of the Constitutional Court Tone Jerovsek in order to decide as soon as possible on a candidate for prime minister.
- Slovenian employers and trade unions on Monday signed an amendment to their collective agreement, prolonging an accord determining work benefits until the end of May 1997.
- President Kucan held a reception on Monday for the highest officers in Slovenia's army and police, marking the sixth anniversary of the nation's decision to separate from former Yugoslavia.
- The Slovenian government has refused to increase postage prices by the requested 25 percent.

- Prime Minister Janez Drnovsek met representatives of the Slovenian Nationalist Party to discuss ways out of the political uncertainty after November's general election. The Nationalists got four out of 90 parliamentary seats.
- Slovenia's Apartment Fund on Monday agreed to raise the amount of money dedicated to apartment loans to 3.2 billion tolars ($22.7 million) from two billion.
- Slovenia's Tourist Association said it managed to achieve over 90 percent of its plans.
- Next year's European month of culture will be held in Ljubljana from May 15 until June 30. In these 45 days some 200 cultural events will take place.
- Slovenia's November industrial output rose 3.6 percent compared to the same month of the previous year, the Statistical Office said on Monday.
